also: worktree whose only blocker is ignored files
remote branch merged only into the local branch

expected: The preview ends with ONE_SHOT (one run of the recommended command reaches the end state), PARTIAL (something remains that no flag lifts) or BLOCKED (a gate fails and nothing can run); the verdict judges the recommended command, not the command as typed.

The end state is only main and <branch> as local branches, the worktrees of the deleted branches removed, and every remote branch deleted or NOT_TOUCHED; it leaves out a worktree the command never touches (a detached one, or one that holds main or another kept branch), and the report lists it.

The recommended command is the /GitSweep <branch> --apply line, with --remote and --lang as given, and exactly the flags that lift something: --discard-ignored with the ignored paths it deletes listed, --push (whether or not it was typed) when a remote branch is PUSH_THEN_DELETE, and also a typed --push whose publish prediction says the push will run, with the publish prediction; a typed --push that cannot run is dropped from the line and the report says why; otherwise a flag that lifts nothing is never recommended and none is added silently.

Every failed gate is reported at once with its remedy, in /GitConverge and in /GitSweep (a --remote that git remote does not list included), and every blocker, UNKNOWN, PREDICTED_CONFLICT and PREDICTED_IGNORED_OVERLAP is followed by the action that lifts it.

A PUSH_THEN_DELETE branch kept for want of --push has the remedy rerun with --push (the Next preview: line, then the Next command: line) or, once local <branch> holds its tip, push <branch> by hand; a PENDING_PUSH branch has the remedy clear the condition the report names (publish the remote default by hand, fetch and merge a newer remote tip, or the rows of an UNKNOWN phase 2); a KEPT_NOT_MERGED branch is merged by the user and then recommended with --apply --push by the next preview.

The apply report ends with the run state COMPLETE or PARTIAL and, for PARTIAL, two lines in this order: Next preview: (the same line without --apply, so that the preview becomes the earlier plan after the remedies) and Next command: (the line to run after that preview; when the preview recommends another line, run the recommended one). Both carry --remote and --lang as given and their flags in the order --apply, --discard-ignored, --push, --remote, --lang; Next command: carries --push when a remote branch ended PUSH_THEN_DELETE or PENDING_PUSH for a reason that a rerun with --push can clear, or when --push was typed and the publish prediction says the push would still run, never when the only reason is that <branch> is the remote default, and with phase 2 UNKNOWN only when it was typed; both lines are left out when no rerun would change anything.

A preview computes the remote classification and the will-remain set as if the recommended command had been typed (a worktree whose only blocker is ignored files counts as lifted when --discard-ignored is recommended), and an apply uses the flags it was given.

### Remedies

Every failed gate, delete blocker, `UNKNOWN` status, `PREDICTED_CONFLICT`, `PREDICTED_IGNORED_OVERLAP`, and stop of an apply (a conflict, an ignored-file overlap, a refused switch, a failed merge or check) in a report is followed by the action that lifts it.
Every gate is evaluated, and the report names every failed gate with its remedy (**Remedies** below), so one run shows everything the user must clear before the next one.
| gate: target is `main` | name the integration branch instead of `main` |
| gate: invoking worktree dirty | commit the changes, or `git stash push --include-untracked`; `git status --short --untracked-files=all` lists what counts |
| `BLOCKED_IGNORED_FILES` | add `--discard-ignored` (the listed files are lost) or move the files out of the worktree |
| `BLOCKED_UPSTREAM_OF_KEPT` | `git branch --unset-upstream <x>` on the branch that tracks it, or retarget that branch |
| `PREDICTED_CONFLICT` | merge that source into the target by hand and resolve it (`git merge refs/heads/<source>`), then rerun; a conflict stops the apply |
| `UNKNOWN` | establish the fact its evidence names; for a case collision, the rename procedure |
A report with a failed gate has no plan: the rest of the preview is not made.
**Remaining items.** For `PARTIAL`, every item that stays: the branch or worktree, its classification, its evidence, its remedy and whether the user must rerun afterwards.
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN`: remote default unknown | `git remote set-head <remote> --auto` |
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN`: no `refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/<remote>/*` mapping | `git config --add remote.<remote>.fetch '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/<remote>/*'`, then `git fetch <remote>` |

| phase 2 `UNKNOWN`: the remote has several URLs, or a push URL that differs from the fetch URL | leave exactly one URL, the same for fetch and push: `git remote set-url --delete <remote> <extra-url>` for each extra URL, and for a separate push URL `git config --unset-all remote.<remote>.pushurl` |
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN` or `STALE` after the live check | `git fetch <remote>` (and `git remote set-head <remote> --auto` when the default changed), then rerun |
| gate: `--remote <name>` not listed by `git remote` | name a listed remote (`git remote -v`), or add it with `git remote add <name> <url>` |

| `PUSH_THEN_DELETE` (kept: `--push` not typed) | rerun with `--push` (the `Next preview:` line, then the `Next command:` line), or publish `<branch>` yourself (`git push <remote> refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>`; local `<branch>` holds the tip after phase 1), then rerun |

| `PENDING_PUSH` | clear the condition the report names, then rerun: if `<branch>` is the remote default, publish it by hand or through your review process (the command never pushes the remote default); if the remote tip is not an ancestor, `git fetch <remote>` and merge it into `<branch>`, then rerun with `--push`; if the push failed or was refused, satisfy the host's rule (branch protection, a hook) and rerun with `--push`, or publish by hand; if phase 2 is `UNKNOWN`, see its rows |

| `PUSH_SKIPPED`, `PUSH_FAILED`, `PUSH_UNCONFIRMED` | clear the named condition: fetch and merge a newer remote tip; satisfy the host's branch protection or hook; fix the failed validation (see the failed-check row); for `<branch>` being `main` or the remote default, publish it by hand or through your review process; or publish by hand, then rerun |
| `KEPT_LOCAL` | clear the local blocker named for that branch |
| `BLOCKED_UPSTREAM` | `git branch --unset-upstream <x>` on the local branch that tracks it |

| `KEPT_NOT_MERGED` | review it and merge it into `<branch>`, or delete it on the host yourself; the command never deletes it. After the merge, the preview lists the branch as `PUSH_THEN_DELETE` and recommends `--apply --push` (as `PENDING_PUSH` with its condition when the publish is not predicted to run) |
| `BLOCKED_BAD_NAME` | delete or rename it on the host |
